reasoning_steps: Identify the right triangle ABC with angles 30°, 60°, and 90°.
Note that the hypotenuse of the triangle is AB, which measures 1 unit.
The circle is tangent to both the x-axis and y-axis, indicating that the radius of the circle is equal to the distance from the origin to the point of tangency.
Since the circle is tangent to the hypotenuse, the radius of the circle is half the length of the hypotenuse.
Calculate the radius by dividing the length of the hypotenuse by 2.
Determine the radius of the circle to be 0.5 units.
